findings.title: Gemini 4 Carbon: our next frontier model
findings.summary_md: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon on October 28, 2026, describing it as its strongest model with state-of-the-art cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. The post reports 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71.0% on Collinear's CWE-bench, and says access starts this week for a subset of cyber defenders before phased rollout to trusted partners through the Fairwind Program. Pricing is set at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, matching Argon's introductory price.

findings.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon with significant gains across coding and agentic tasks
findings.summary_md: 9to5Google reported the announcement on October 28, 2026, noting Carbon ranks first on v5.0 of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with a score of 59 and that Google attributes the fast release to researchers and models working together. The article repeats the benchmark figures of 88.2% on SEC-bench Pro, 54.8% on ExploitGym, and 71.0% on CWE-bench, and notes the rollout begins this week with cyber defenders. It adds that Carbon improves by 89 Elo points to fourth place on WebDev Arena.

findings.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Carbon with a significant leap in cybersecurity
findings.summary_md: The Verge reported on October 28, 2026 that Gemini 4 Carbon outperforms Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra on some benchmarks and holds the top spot on SEC-bench Pro and ExploitGym. The article notes Carbon improves on Argon, released earlier in October 2026, and is initially limited to select cybersecurity defense companies before expanding through Fairwind. Google frames the model as a significant leap in cyberdefense for finding vulnerabilities and generating secure code.
